toEnglish.explanation: S O V order. tusa-tusa = PL~navigator; tunaka = soldier; tamika-xi-mi = temple-POSS-ACC; ki = NEG; muka-ta-ba = bless-PST-3PL.

toLang.prompt: The king did not guard the navigators' temple.
toLang.explanation: S O V order. tana = king; tusa-tusa = PL~navigator; tamika-xi-mi = temple-POSS-ACC; ki = NEG; sipa-ta = guard-PST.

grammar: Word order: subject, object, verb. With one participant: subject, verb.
Plural: say the noun twice (tamika → tamika-tamika).
Marks the possessed noun (“the king's horse” = king horse-POSS). The possessor itself is bare.
Past tense. Without it the verb is present or future.
On the verb when the subject is plural.
Negation: a separate word before the verb.
Come after the noun. Noun endings go on the noun only; the adjective stays bare.
explain.notes: Checked against 1557 alternative analyses; the sentences rule out 1544, including: -ta appears when: past & plural subject.
